This page collects gaps and open questions in the ''Star Wars CCG'' rules that may need a ruling in the future. It is a working list, not a set of official rules. Each entry shows what [[Decipher Comprehensive Rules|Decipher's rules]] and the [[Players Committee Advanced Rulebook]] say, and what is still unanswered.

== Open gaps ==

=== Imprisoned captives at a site that stops being a prison ===
'''Example:''' [[Arena Execution]] (Virtual Block 9, Dark) makes Petranaki Arena a prison. Its "Turn the Tide" text places it in the Used Pile if the opponent controls Petranaki Arena during their control phase. The same card lets that opponent release any number of captives there during their control phase. Both happen during the Light Side's control phase, so the Light Side chooses the order. If the Light Side lets the Mission go first, captives can be left imprisoned at a site that is no longer a prison.

'''What the rules say:'''
* Neither rulebook says what happens to captives imprisoned at a site that stops being a prison.
* Controlling a prison does not release imprisoned captives. The Players Committee rulebook example: Leia controls Detention Block Corridor but still needs a card such as [[Someone Who Loves You]] to release Han. Under Decipher's rules, [[Death Star: Detention Block Control Room]]'s Light Side text is a specific card effect, not a general rule.

'''Why the board state is not stuck:''' if the captives remain imprisoned captives at that site, the Light Side can still free them with:
* [[Captive Pursuit]] (any captive present at a site where a battle was just initiated)
* [[8D8]] (any imprisoned captive with 8D8)
* [[Commander Ruescott Melshi]] (an imprisoned captive at his site)
* [[Someone Who Loves You]] (Han only)
* [[Rescue On Geonosis]] keeps Petranaki Arena a prison, so the situation does not arise while it is on table.
Cards that need a prison ([[Jedi Mind Trick]]) or a specific site (Detention Block Corridor, Blockade Flagship: Prison) do not reach these captives.

'''Possible future ruling:''' state that captives remain imprisoned captives at a site that stops being a prison (no automatic release). GEMP plays it this way today and lets the Light Side choose the order.

=== Two "even if ... may not normally be ..." cards ===
Some cards override a restriction "even if" it would normally apply, for example [[Field Dressing]] ("forfeit = 0 ... even if forfeit may not normally be reduced") against Emperor's Sinister Plans ("your spies may not have their forfeit reduced below 3"). Field Dressing wins that pair. No rule covers two cards that both use "even if ... may not normally be ..." language against each other. A timing rule (for example, the most recent effect wins) would be needed if such a pair appears.

== Rulings adopted in GEMP ==

=== Same-side games: tied first-turn claims ===
In GEMP games where both players play the same side, starting cards can give equal and opposite first-turn claims (both players start with Death Star, or both with Massassi Throne Room, or an equivalent pair). In that case a coin toss decides who takes the first turn.
